Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 3-day history of watery, loose stools occurring 6–7×/day; associated left-sided lower-abdominal crampy pain.
- Associated symptoms:
  • Initial vomiting at symptom onset (resolved).  
  • Subjective fever 3–4 days ago; currently afebrile.  
  • Weakness, shakiness, decreased appetite; able to tolerate oral fluids (soups, smoothies).  
  • No blood in stool or vomitus; no night sweats.
- Potential trigger: Chinese restaurant takeaway 4 days ago; no similar illness in household (one child vomited once, no diarrhea).
- Impact on life: Must stay near toilet; continues working as an accountant but with difficulty.
- Past medical history: Asthma (well-controlled with inhaler).
- Medications: Asthma inhaler (type/dose/frequency not documented); no other regular medications.
- Social history: Lives with wife and two children; non-smoker; does not consume alcohol.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
- No physical examination performed during consult.
- No vital signs or investigations available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrhea with abdominal pain
   - Assessment: Likely acute infectious gastroenteritis (viral > bacterial).
   - Differential diagnosis: Foodborne bacterial infection; less likely inflammatory bowel disease, medication-induced diarrhea.
   - Investigations planned: None at present; stool culture if symptoms persist >3–4 days.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Oral rehydration with water and commercial electrolyte solution (e.g., Dioralyte).  
     • Paracetamol 500 mg–1 g orally up to 4×/day PRN for fever or discomfort (dose/route/frequency per OTC guidance).  
     • Rest and abstain from work for 2–3 days.  
     • Dietary advice: light, easily digestible foods; avoid dairy, caffeine, alcohol.  
   - Follow-up: Re-evaluate if no improvement or worsening in 3–4 days, or sooner for red-flag symptoms (blood in stool, high fever, persistent vomiting, signs of dehydration).

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: allergies not documented; type/dose/frequency of asthma inhaler not documented; no vital signs or physical examination recorded.  
● Internal conflicts: none identified.  
● Transcript quality: clear; minor conversational interruptions, no significant inaudible sections.
